Connected workflows and record contracts

The HTML prototype must keep one consistent fictional record across views. Scenario switches may construct alternate worlds, but clicking through a normal journey must not unexpectedly substitute a different learner, course, deadline or attempt. The records below describe frontend/domain contracts, not a prescribed backend schema.

Record inventory

RecordMinimum meaningful fields
Person / course enrollmentStable person ID, display name, institutional email, course offering ID, role, active window, permitted actions and assigned grading scope.
Course offeringCode/title, institution/term/section, zone, instructors, publish/access/archive state, syllabus/policy version, modules, tool access references.
Module / materialStable ID, order, title, type, body/asset version, publication, releaseAt, prerequisite, accessible alternative; per-learner completion is separate.
AssessmentStable ID, type, title/instructions version, points, category, published audience, due/close, allowed formats/size, attempts, rubric version, AI policy and group set if used.
Quiz / attemptIndependent quiz close/due, time limit, allowance, attempt rule, immutable item/settings snapshot, answers by item ID, save acknowledgment and submit receipt.
Submission / receiptCourse/assessment/learner or group ID, attempt, submitted version, ordered files/pages/tags, actor, accepted time, receipt reference and membership snapshot.
Score/reviewAssessment/attempt/person/question IDs, rubric/manual source, current draft score, comments, reviewed question IDs, reviewer and revision/conflict history.
Release snapshotApproved exact recipients and candidate kind; actual attempt/receipt and rubric when applicable, score/comments or status, policy version, author/time, exclusions, fingerprint and prior release IDs.
Grading policyVersion, points/weighted mode, categories and item membership, within-category method, weights, empty/ungraded/missing/excused rules, rounding and letter boundaries.
Group set / membershipPurpose/course, group IDs, names, members, assigned assessment IDs, self-enrollment rules/window, membership versions and change history.
AllowancePerson/course/assessment, adjusted due/close/timer/attempt rule, author/time, minimal private basis reference restricted to instructor. No medical attachment.
Calendar itemID/source owner, visibility, course/person, start/end/zone or all-day dates, recurrence ID/exception, publication/version, reminder preference reference.
Grading taskAssigned TA/assessment/learner/question scope, target deadline, allocated/remaining work, progress and access window.
Announcement / discussionCourse/audience, author, draft/published/scheduled status, content version, attachments, post/edit times, moderation reasons and reply availability.
ActivitySource record/version, safe title, audience, unread state, event time and destination. Keep visible feed separate from email/push delivery.
Tool / technical requestVerified access/eligibility/help metadata; request ID, user-provided description, explicitly selected diagnostics and attachment status.
Copy/import previewSource/destination content, mapping, excluded learner records, warnings/blockers, changes/fingerprint, owner review and applied result.

In the prototype, IDs/version checks may be ordinary JS state. Future services must enforce them with real authorization, concurrency, storage and audit. Do not design the UI around unsafe assumptions that all clients can read the complete course data.

Critical journeys

  1. Arrival: W01 institution handoff, W02 return/recovery, W03 invitation when present, W04 role/context onboarding, W05 home. Wrong institution/account never activates an invitation; repeated valid acceptance does not duplicate access.
  2. Individual work: W06/W14 course, W16/W17 material, W18/W19 assignment, W20 add work, W21 review, W22 received receipt. Closing an upload or scanning a page does not submit. Final send needs a clear acknowledgment; interrupted/queued remains unreceived.
  3. Grade and release: W48 queue, W49 assigned evidence/questions, W50 impact when needed, W51 staff calculation, W53 exact release, W23/W24 learner results. Saving scores does not certify complete review. A stale preview blocks release. TAs cannot release even through a deep link.
  4. Course setup: W35 builder, W36 syllabus/settings, W37 module, W38 lesson/W39 assets, W40 assignment/W41 quiz and W43/W44 rubric, then publication and student preview W14. Publish validates relevant dates, points, audiences and accessible alternatives.
  5. Quiz: W25 rules, W26 start/save/recovery, W27 receipt, then results according to captured release policy. Author edits after submission cannot change captured question text/options/answers/settings. A fresh authorized attempt uses current settings without destroying prior attempts.
  6. Policy/grades: W52 configure and preview, W51 staff view, W24 released learner view, W54 corrections where needed. Every displayed total must state what is included and which policy/release is used.
  7. Group work: W47 groups, W40 assignment targeting, W33/W34 membership/workspace, W19-W22 shared attempt, W49 grade with group/individual effects, W53 release, W24 individual visibility. A member submits on behalf of a known group; others see the same received version and actor. Post-submission membership changes do not silently redistribute old work/grades.
  8. TA workload: W45 role/scope, W57 allocation/deadline, W05 TA home/W07 calendar, W48 queue, W49 review. Ended access changes actions immediately; original attributed scores stay. Progress is derived from actual assigned review, not page visits.
  9. Communication: W55 draft/schedule/publish, W28/W29 read, W08 notice, W30/W31 discussion and W56 moderation. Drafts never notify students. A hidden post retains author/staff history with role-safe explanations.
  10. Calendar: W32 course events and office hours, W07 combined view/private planning, W08 reminders/preferences. Published events share one ID across views; moving a course event invalidates its earlier reminder. Read-only source meetings cannot be edited as private events.
  11. Exceptions: W46 applies a scoped allowance, W19/W25 show personal rules, W58 attendance correction preserves original evidence, W54 reviews a grade concern without private messaging. Keep student-visible explanation separate from restricted basis/reference.
  12. Term continuity: W06 archive, W59 copy and W60 content import/export. New offering is draft and distinct from original; people, submissions, grades, private discussions, allowances and attendance are not copied as course content.

data/journeys.json lists these as page-ID sequences for implementation tracking. Optional features must not be required to complete them.

Grade calculations and release visibility

Proposed first implementation supports points and category-weighted modes. Advanced custom formulas remain a later decision. Within a weighted category, use proportional points by default; if the instructor selects equal assessment weighting, average each assessment's percentage instead. Do not confuse the two methods.

Weights must total 100% before a weighted policy can be published. Validate finite non-negative values and a named category for every included item; prevent duplicated contribution. An exempt item is removed from numerator and denominator. Received-but-ungraded work is excluded. A course-defined missing item can count zero after close, but learner visibility still follows release. Zero possible points must not cause division by zero. Extra credit needs an explicit rule; leave disabled by default in the first HTML until selected.

For empty categories, proposed default is to redistribute active-category weights proportionally and display “Current grade based on released work”; if all categories are empty, display “No released grade yet.” Also show planned total weight represented so students do not mistake a running grade for a final grade. Test one empty category and all-empty categories with an explicit denominator in each example. The institution can choose a different policy before production.

Round display only at the final step, proposed two decimal places; do not round intermediate category values. Letter ranges must be non-overlapping and cover the selected scale. A policy change after publication needs old/new previews and a new version. It must not silently rewrite already-released feedback snapshots or official records. Whether a new course total itself needs explicit publication is a policy decision: first HTML retains a released learner projection until the instructor confirms the new policy/result projection.

Fixture check: under the accepted example category mix Assignments 40%, Labs 25%, Quizzes 35%, Aisha's released assignment marks 24/30 and 27/30 give 85%; an excused 30-point item is excluded; labs 18/20 give 90%; quiz 8/10 gives 80%. Released course grade = 84.50%. A held PS4 score 27/30 makes the staff calculation 85.1666...%, displayed 85.17%, while the learner remains at 84.50%. Only releasing the new result/projection changes the learner total. data/fixtures.json includes these golden values and a separate configurable 10/25/25/40 example.

Submission and group invariants

  • Received attempts are immutable. A new attempt starts from a copied draft with a new ID/attempt number; old receipt/files/comments remain inspectable under the right permissions.
  • Review includes page order, orientation, question coverage and file readability. Unsupported/corrupt/oversized examples fail with file-specific recovery. Do not claim OCR accuracy or actual malware scanning in HTML.
  • Group receipt names the group, submitting actor, version and recipient membership at acceptance. Duplicate concurrent send reuses the accepted result or asks to refresh; never manufactures two successful attempts from one action.
  • Changing membership while a draft exists warns about access and ownership. Once received, old membership/recipients remain historical. Late join/withdrawal/individual overrides need an explicit instructor decision and audit trail; no automatic retroactive distribution.
  • Grade correction creates a draft revision with old/new comparison and a reason. Earlier releases remain available; learner feedback changes only when a new version is released. Do not rescore manually overridden answers through a bulk rubric rule.

Quiz, copy and integration limits

Quiz save timestamps describe acknowledged state. Proposed timing default: the effective deadline is the earlier of personal close and startedAt plus the effective timer duration; an untimed quiz still ends at personal close. An allowance uses either extra minutes or a multiplier, never both implicitly. Show the available duration before Start if close truncates the timer. At expiry, finalize acknowledged answers once; keep unacknowledged offline edits as an explicitly unsent local draft for recovery/staff review. A frontend cannot guarantee acceptance past the authoritative close or manufacture an accepted timestamp. Specify resume/time-expiry/conflict screens and validate high-stakes adjudication with the institution before production. Never reset time by refreshing, infer cheating from blur, or erase work because a window changed.

Fixtures include separate before-close assignment/group scenarios and a late-start quiz scenario. The default Oct 20 world already contains received PS4 work; do not use it unchanged to demonstrate a fresh first submission. Apply both the scenario clock and named record resets, then complete the normal workflow.

Copy/import runs against an exact current preview. Changing source file, mapping, selected assets or target dates invalidates acceptance. Unsupported question/tool/media types remain visible blockers or acknowledged placeholders. Export/download is a local fictional sample in HTML; it does not send official grades to an SIS. LTI services and content formats require selected versions and real integration work later. [M06](../research/core-evidence.md).
